aggregate_criterion_inherited_from_v01.G_pres_subset_a_a_relative: Arm M within-Recon mean 4-dim Manhattan distance from the per-evaluator reference vector <= Arm C within-Recon mean 4-dim Manhattan distance from the same reference vector + 1.5

aggregate_criterion_inherited_from_v01.scope_note_pi_freeze_correction_1_C_minu: The +1.5 Manhattan tolerance applies ONLY to G_pres_subset_a_a. Arm-C validity envelope (C20) is not enlarged by this tolerance.

non_collapse_attestation_v4: The 4 dimensions in subset-(a) are evaluated via the aggregate 4-dim Manhattan criterion. Subset-(a) is a SEPARATE PRESERVATION FAMILY from subset-(b) (the 8 C12 axes). The two subsets are kept disjoint by ID namespace (BIB-4D-* vs C12-*) and by criterion (Manhattan aggregate vs per-axis binary-failure). The v4 protocol EXPLICITLY does NOT invent any one-to-one semantic identity between the subset-(a) BIB 4-dim dimensions and any subset-(b) C12 axis, even where the display names happen to coincide in unrelated v0.1 §11.3 prose (e.g., 'selection significance' as C12-3, 'factual discipline' as C12-7). The calibrated 4-dim vector IS the BIB rubric's 4-dim; the C12 axes ARE the v0.1 §11.3 8 axes; they are measured by different scorebooks (or the same scorebook producing both score vectors), reported as separate gates, and adjudicated under separate criteria.
